Database relations

MTL Explorer uses PostgreSQL with PostGIS. These diagrams cover all 38 foreign keys and list all 42 application tables in the schema through Liquibase change 111. Table names without a schema prefix belong to public. Only keys and selected fields are shown; the Liquibase changelog defines the complete schema.

Reading the diagrams

Every line represents an enforced foreign key; its label names the child column. PK means primary key and FK means foreign key. UK marks a unique key; multiple fields marked UK in a table form one composite key. A circle means zero is allowed, a bar means one, and a crow's foot means many. Cardinalities describe what the database allows. Solid lines use a foreign key as part of the child's primary key; dashed lines use a separate key. Nullable fields are noted where they affect a relationship.

Tracks and derived data

Mermaid source.

An indexed file can produce several tracks. duplicate_of and source_parent_track_id reference other rows in gps_track. Track geometry, point calculations, and events are stored separately. Saved plans also use gps_track; track_source distinguishes their origin. See GPS processing.

The database owns gps_track.version. Metadata writes increment it, and statement triggers on gps_track_data also revise each affected parent once per statement when stored geometry variants are inserted, updated, moved or deleted. An import inserts each geometry variant separately, so it advances the version several times. Version-only updates do not create metadata audit snapshots (change 112). Individual point writes do not invoke these triggers. This lets the client reuse unchanged track caches while refreshing metadata and all geometry precisions for revised tracks. See change 111.

Cache reuse assumes one database history. The restore procedure rotates the installation identity before startup, including restores to the same address. Browsers also discard the cache when a freshness revision decreases. An unannounced restore whose counters have already caught up cannot be detected from IDs and versions alone; rotating the identity is required.

Source review and acknowledgements

Mermaid source.

Source reviews, use decisions, and issues refer to the indexed file. An issue can have one acknowledgement per account_key; that key is an authenticated account name, with no database account table. See source issues.

Media and track correlation

Mermaid source.

Media and tracks are related through media_track_correlation. Its composite unique key permits one candidate per media/track pair. A partial unique index allows at most one selected candidate per media file. Corrections, resolved locations, calculation state, and work queues have at most one row per owning media file or track. See media correlation.

Google Health records and route ownership

Mermaid source.

The google_health schema isolates connection state and imported Health records. connection.id is constrained to 1. Routes can refer to normal indexed files and GPS tracks; deletion of those public rows sets the Health references to null. Deleting a connection cascades to sync_state, data_source, data_point, and heart_rate_sample. The route_ownership connection reference has no cascade.

Heart-rate identity uniqueness uses partial indexes: named records use (connection_id, identity_key) and unnamed records use (connection_id, sample_time, identity_key). These are omitted from the field key markers. See Health synchronization.

Google Health synchronization work

Mermaid source.

history_child.parent_id is the only foreign key in this group. Account-scoped tables share the Google account ID by application convention. Their account_id columns have no foreign key to connection.google_user_id or sync_control. history_audit.work_id and traversal_ids retain logical work/traversal references without foreign keys.

Client login and request logs

Mermaid source.

Both log tables reference the unique client_login_ref, rather than the login row's id. A log may have no login reference. The login's last-log IDs are application links without foreign keys. system_log.client_login_ref also has no foreign key. Its nullable stack_fingerprint has a non-unique index and is calculated from the full captured stack when a client report is submitted. Existing rows retain null. See diagnostic logging.

Tables without foreign keys

These nine public tables complete the application table inventory.

Table Purpose
config Stored settings, keyed by id
filter_config Filter definitions, keyed by id
data_freshness Domain revisions, keyed by domain_key
system_log Server and client diagnostics, keyed by id
indexed_file_audit Indexed-file change snapshots
gps_track_audit Track change snapshots
media_file_audit Media change snapshots
config_audit Setting change snapshots
filter_config_audit Filter change snapshots

Audit tables retain copied IDs and values without primary or foreign keys. They can retain history after deletion of the source row.

Views and infrastructure

gps_track_v joins tracks, indexed-file metadata, and derived geometry. media_file_v joins media and indexed-file metadata. These are query views, with no independent primary or foreign keys.

Liquibase's databasechangelog and databasechangeloglock, PostGIS's spatial_ref_sys, and the PostGIS metadata views are excluded from the application table count.

Diagram editing and rendering are described in the asset notes.

Read-only database access

Dynamic SQL uses the separate mtluserreadonly pool. New databases create the role without a password. After Liquibase completes, startup applies MTL_DB_READONLY_PASSWORD before opening that pool. An unset or blank value uses the configured primary database password. PostgreSQL quotes both the role and credential; the credential is excluded from startup diagnostics. Existing databases use the same startup path. The table and relation diagrams are unchanged.
